title: planqc Expands into the UK with Double-Digit Million-Euro Cambridge Optical-Lattice Facility - Quantum Computing Report
gist: German neutral-atom quantum company planqc has set up planqc UK Ltd with a double-digit million-euro investment in a Cambridge assembly, integration and commissioning lab. The lab is backed by Arm co-founder Hermann Hauser and partnered with the Cavendish Laboratory to develop optical-lattice architectures meant to scale neutral-atom processors toward millions of qubits. The move also puts planqc closer to finance and pharma users in London and Cambridge.

themes.theme: planqc UK subsidiary and Cambridge lab

insights.claim: Neutral-atom quantum computing company planqc has created a UK subsidiary, planqc UK Ltd, backed by a double-digit million-euro investment to build an assembly, integration and commissioning laboratory in Cambridge.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A private neutral-atom player is spending real money on international hardware capacity, which suggests it has funding headroom and is pushing to commercialize.
insights.locator: German neutral-atom quantum computing company planqc

insights.claim: planqc's Cambridge facility will house laser and optical subsystems, and over the next two years it plans to hire quantum hardware, error-correction, FPGA and software engineers there.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The hiring plan points to demand for quantum hardware and control-electronics talent in the Cambridge cluster.
insights.locator: German neutral-atom quantum computing company planqc

insights.claim: Arm and Amadeus Capital Partners co-founder Hermann Hauser, an investor in planqc and a member of its board, is supporting the UK expansion. The subsidiary is led by planqc co-founders Sebastian Blatt and Alexander Glätzle.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Backing from a well-connected UK tech investor could help planqc reach UK capital and partners.
insights.locator: Led by planqc co-founders Dr. Sebastian Blatt

insights.claim: planqc's Cambridge team, working with Professor Ulrich Schneider's group at the University of Cambridge's Cavendish Laboratory, will develop optical-lattice architectures. These use overlapping laser beams to create periodic trapping arrays, with the aim of scaling neutral-atom processors toward millions of qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Optical lattices are planqc's bet on how to reach million-qubit scale, so watch for lattice-based qubit-count milestones compared with other neutral-atom approaches.
insights.quote: capable of scaling neutral-atom processors toward millions of qubits
insights.locator: In partnership with Professor Ulrich Schneider

insights.claim: After an earlier expansion into Innsbruck, Austria, planqc now has more than 130 employees and over €100 million in combined private funding and public contracts.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: These figures size planqc as one of Europe's larger private quantum hardware companies, and public contracts make up a meaningful part of the funding.
insights.locator: Following earlier expansion into Innsbruck, Austria

insights.claim: planqc's UK site is meant to bring the company closer to financial and pharmaceutical users in London and Cambridge, which signals that these sectors are its target early enterprise customers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Watch for planqc pilot announcements with UK banks or pharma companies.
insights.locator: Following earlier expansion into Innsbruck, Austria
